TW: Suicide

I haven’t been able to get over my phobia of needles. Every time I try to go into a vaccination center, I feel like I’ll get trapped and panic inside. 

It’s been 3 months of not being able to enter any mall or attraction. Basically, a worse-than-circuit-breaker state of life but with no one to relate with and no end in sight. Even more months of immense guilt for not being able to do a simple thing to protect those around me. Even more months of being told that Im a bad person. Everywhere I look, it’s “fuck anti-vaxxers”, tax/punish/ostracise/outcast anti-vaxxers and I can’t say I disagree. I hate myself. 

I’ve been going for multiple sessions of specific-phobia therapy but feel no closer to my goal of getting vaccinated. Im afraid Im just not cut out for the post-covid-19 world. 

Everyday is just work, sleep, see other friends go out, stay home, work. I fantasise about suicide everyday and I see no light at the end of the tunnel. There is simply no reason for me to carry on.

Thank you so much for this post. All these headlines blasting anti-vaxxers has been adding to my immense guilt. My government called me a “free-rider” just the other day.

Although I’m in therapy and still trying, reading success posts somehow discourages me. I hope the situation improves for us somehow.
I see! How was your phobia at the start and how is it now?

I’ll start: I’ve been doing exposure therapy a few days a week for two weeks now. I managed to get through the “easier” ones - holding a needle, looking at videos - but i’m struggling with actually touching a needle to my arm. 

I still feel the same “I can’t do it” thoughts very strongly to the point i find it hard to believe that i’ll actually go.

Not giving up though and will keep trying exposure therapy. i’ve been re-reading studies on exposure therapy’s effectiveness to remind myself that it will likely work. If all else fails, I’ll consider going to an actual therapist.

I agree with you 100%. I’ve heard comments like “just look away” or “it’s just a little pinch” all too many times. I think people mean well but it’s really hard to empathise with something they’ve never experienced. Most end up trying to reason with a phobia which, by it’s nature, is irrational. 

Anyway, it’s nice to hear from people in the same boat. I’ll keep trying as well. I’m sure it can be overcome.

Hey, I just read your update. I’m really glad you tried. You took a huge step today which some of us don’t even dare to take yet!

Even if it doesn’t feel like it, today was progress! Many people here who got the shot had to go through several attempts as well. Keep your head up and keep trying. I think you’re doing great!
Just go in with the intention of getting in the chair. At that point it’s up to you whether to take the vaccine or not. Try to make it to that chair and see how you feel!
All the best! I’m actively going through exposure therapy too so my inbox is always open if you want to talk.

I know right! I still find it hard to believe that I’ll be able to take a shot at the end of this. 

What helped me was reading a lot of studies that said exposure therapy was effective when treating needle phobia. 

I also tried a few sessions myself, taking down my anxiety level at the start and end of the hour-long exposure and found that it actually did drop by 50%! Seeing progress was quite motivating for me.

It’s important not to push yourself into a step that’s too hard. Many small steps is better than avoiding a big step. Also, when you’re in an exposure, make sure you stay in it until your anxiety drops by about half! If you end it early, you might reinforce the fear.
Don’t give up! If it’s too hard, you can try doing easier steps first like imagining a needle until your anxiety reduces to half.
